common_name: Apple Blossom Armand Clematis (Pink-Blushed Evergreen Spring Clematis)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Apple Blossom is a pink-flushed selection of evergreen Armand clematis and, like the species, blooms very early on the previous year's growth, so any pruning to control size should happen right after flowering rather than in late winter.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade against a sturdy trellis, arbor, or fence, since this selection shares the vigorous, large-growing habit of the species. Apple Blossom opens deep pink buds that fade to a soft blush-pink and white as the star-shaped, richly fragrant flowers expand, a warmer color break from the plain white typical of the species, held above the same leathery, glossy evergreen foliage that gives year-round structure. Prune only right after the early spring bloom finishes, since flower buds form on the prior season's wood and later cuts remove the coming display. Established vines tolerate short dry spells but perform best with regular moisture and a mulched, shaded root run.

common_name: Snowdrift Armand Clematis (Compact Pure White Evergreen Spring Clematis)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Snowdrift is a somewhat more compact, pure white-flowered selection of evergreen Armand clematis, still needing a sturdy support but easier to keep in bounds than the vigorous straight species.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade with a trellis, arbor, or fence for support. Snowdrift bears masses of clean white, star-shaped, intensely fragrant flowers over glossy leathery evergreen foliage in early spring, and its somewhat smaller leaves and slightly more restrained growth make it a bit easier to manage on a modest fence or arbor than the species. Because it flowers on the previous year's wood, prune only immediately after blooming to shape the vine, never in late winter. Give it a warm, sheltered spot in colder parts of its range, since flower bud set can be reduced after an unusually cold winter.

planting.note: Plant this Mediterranean evergreen clematis selection in autumn with its roots shaded and cool; Freckles is the most heavily marked of the cirrhosa cultivars, its nodding bells patterned with dense maroon speckling inside.

directions: Plant in autumn with roots shaded and cool while the ferny, bronze-tinted winter foliage climbs into brighter light above. Freckles is the best-known selection of winter clematis, its nodding, bell-shaped, pale cream flowers washed and speckled inside with dense maroon-red spotting that gives each bloom a distinctly hand-painted look, opening from late autumn through winter into early spring when little else is in flower. Holder of a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit, it is a dependable choice for softening a sheltered wall or fence with off-season color. Prune only lightly right after flowering to tidy growth, since the plant sets next winter's buds soon afterward.

common_name: Wisley Cream Clematis (Pale Unspotted Winter-Flowering Evergreen Clematis)

planting.note: Plant this Mediterranean evergreen clematis selection in autumn with its roots shaded and cool; Wisley Cream bears plain, unspotted pale cream bells rather than the maroon freckling typical of many cirrhosa selections.

directions: Plant in autumn with roots shaded and cool while the finely divided, sometimes purple-tinged winter foliage climbs into brighter light above. Wisley Cream, selected at the Royal Horticultural Society's garden of the same name and holder of an Award of Garden Merit, produces nodding, bell-shaped flowers in a soft, even pale cream without the maroon speckling seen in cultivars like 'Freckles', giving it a cleaner, more understated look through its long late-autumn-to-spring bloom season. It is a useful choice where a quieter, monochrome winter flower is preferred over a heavily patterned one. Prune only lightly right after flowering to tidy growth without sacrificing next winter's buds.

common_name: Jingle Bells Clematis (Free-Flowering Compact Winter Evergreen Clematis)

planting.note: Plant this Mediterranean evergreen clematis selection in autumn with its roots shaded and cool; Jingle Bells is a compact, unusually free-flowering cirrhosa selection well suited to a large container or small trellis.

directions: Plant in autumn in a container or against a small trellis with roots shaded and cool, since Jingle Bells stays noticeably more compact than the straight species. From late autumn into late winter it produces an unusually heavy crop of small, nodding, unspotted creamy-white bells over dark, ferny evergreen foliage, sized well for a patio pot or narrow bed rather than the large support most cirrhosa selections need. Bred from Guernsey nursery stock prized for floriferousness, it rewards a sheltered, sunny-headed, cool-rooted position with reliable midwinter color. Prune lightly right after flowering to keep the plant tidy without removing the buds forming for next winter.

planting.note: Plant this Balearic Islands native evergreen clematis in autumn with its roots shaded and cool; the finely dissected, fern-like foliage is the main ornamental feature outside of its winter bloom, bronzing attractively in cold weather.

directions: Plant in autumn with roots shaded and cool while the finely cut, almost parsley-like evergreen foliage climbs into brighter light above, where cold weather turns the leaves an attractive bronze-purple through winter. This botanical variety, native to Spain's Balearic Islands, bears small, nodding, pale yellow bells lightly spotted red-purple inside from late autumn into early spring, produced against foliage that is arguably more distinctive than the flowers themselves. It is a good choice for adding textured, off-season interest to a sheltered wall or fence in mild-winter gardens. Prune only lightly right after flowering, since it sets next winter's flower buds on the current season's growth soon after bloom ends.

planting.note: Plant this Himalayan species in autumn with roots shaded and cool; unlike most clematis, Nepal clematis drops its leaves and rests through summer heat, then leafs out and flowers again from fall into winter.

directions: Plant in autumn with roots shaded and cool on a fence, wall, or shrub for support, in a mild, sheltered microclimate. Native to the Himalayan foothills of Nepal, this clematis follows an unusual reversed growth cycle among vines cultivated for winter interest: it goes dormant and drops its leaves during summer heat, then breaks new growth in fall and flowers from late autumn into winter, opening small, nodding, pale cream bells with prominent dark purple stamens and a light fragrance. Because summer dormancy is normal rather than a sign of trouble, withhold heavy watering once the foliage drops and resume as new growth emerges in autumn. It suits the same mild, well-drained, winter-garden niche as Clematis cirrhosa but offers a distinct bloom form and an even more tender constitution, so it is best reserved for the warmer end of its hardiness range.
